title: Traffic Stabilization Protocol and Cross-functional Collaboration Checklist (WIP)
body:
Purpose
This doc captures a pragmatic, cross-functional protocol for stabilizing traffic during phased rollouts and A/B experiments. Focus is on small, repeatable steps teams can use when pushing inference-related changes (model variants, routing rules, batching/quantization toggles) so we avoid oscillations and minimize user impact.

Scope
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (where teams control routing).
- Intended for mid-to-large scale traffic slices (0.5% to 30%). Not a binary feature flag playbook — assumes observable token-level metrics and model variants.

Key principles
- Short window, clear guardrails: each increment has a deterministic observation window and gating metric set.
- Single decision owner per slice: one product/PM or eng lead signs off.
- Fail fast, revert safely: automated quick-revert paths and pre-wired fallback models.
- Communication first: pre-scheduled notices, Slack incident channel, on-call aware.

Actors & responsibilities
- Product Lead (PL): hypothesis, success criteria, user cohorts.
- Experiment Owner (EO, usually eng or ML eng): implements routing changes, toggles, and measurement hooks.
- SRE / Infra: ensures autoscaling and capacity buffers, validates rollout automation.
- Observability / Platform Analytics: sets dashboards, real-time alerts, and sampling hooks.
- CS / Support: preps canned responses and triage playbooks.
- Legal / Security (if needed): approves data paths and telemetry.

Stabilization cadence (recommended)
1) Pre-warm (0% -> 0.5%): 30m observation, validate latency P50/P95, error-rate, and token-cost delta.
2) Micro-increase (0.5% -> 2%): 1h observation. Check model quality via sampled hallucination/regression tests and eval prompt set.
3) Small-bump (2% -> 10%): 3h observation with autoscaling check and cold-start monitoring.
4) Broading (10% -> 30%): 6h observation and progressive traffic smoothing (max step = 10% per bump).

Gating metrics (primary + secondary)
Primary (must be green):
- End-to-end success rate (call-level): >= baseline - 0.5ppt
- Latency P95: <= baseline * 1.25 or absolute cap (e.g., 1.5s)
- Token cost per request: within budget delta (pre-committed)

Secondary (investigate if drift):
- Quality regressions on control prompt set (score drop > 3 points)
- Memory/KV cache hit rate changes
- Increased retry/backoff rate

Alerting & thresholds
- Immediate page (SRE on-call) if success rate drops > 1.5ppt or P95 increases > 50% vs baseline during observation window.
- Slack alert to #rollouts for softer thresholds (0.5ppt, 25% P95 increase).

Traffic partitioning heuristics
- Start with orthogonal slices (region, user-tier, client-version) to limit correlated failure modes.
- Prefer user-id modulo slices for even distribution when client signals matter.
- When testing model variants that change tokenization/lengths, slice by request-size buckets to avoid mixing distributions.

Experiment analysis checklist (during window)
- Verify telemetry ingestion (sampling rate consistent).
- Run automated evals on 1k sampled responses vs control set.
- Check cost attribution per token and per-request.
- Confirm no skew in affected endpoints (e.g., embeddings vs chat).
- Validate model-fallback paths exercised in test harness.

Rollback & fallback patterns
- Immediate rollback: revert routing via control-plane toggle (target < 60s). Document who executes.
- Passive fallback: route degraded traffic to safer model variant or regional fallback.
- Gradual degrade: apply rate-limiting to experimental slice if partial issues detected.

Comms kit (templates)
- Pre-launch: short note to #rollouts and SRE 24h prior with intent, hypothesis, and rollback owner.
- Launch Slack: single-line status update at each bump (0.5% -> 2% -> 10%...). Include metrics snapshot and next step ETA.
- Incident: create channel #inc-rollout-<id>, tag on-call, PL, EO, and CS lead.

Short sample Slack pre-launch
"PL/EO: planning a model routing bump for search-quality experiment tomorrow 09:00 UTC. 0->0.5% then progressive steps. EO: @LiamO. SRE: @oncall. Rollback owner: @Aisha. Dashboards: <link>."

Data & statistical considerations
- Use randomized assignment within slice. Record assignment for reproducibility.
- Prefer Bayesian interval checks for small slices to avoid overconfident p-values.
- Always report base rates and absolute differences, not just percentage change.
- For quality signals with high variance (human evals), extend observation windows or increase sample size before expanding.

Post-experiment hygiene
- Postmortem template filled within 72h if any page/alert fired.
- Archive exact routing config + timestamped snapshots of model binaries and quantization flags.
- Cost reconciliation against predicted delta.

Operational checklists (quick)
- Pre-launch: capacity check, dashboard links, owner list, rollback steps documented, contact list pinned.
- During window: minute-0, minute-15, minute-60, hourly checks with logs attached.
- Post-window: decision recorded (promote, hold, rollback), update product roadmap tickets.

Open questions / TODOs
- Formalize the gating metric thresholds per product line (hosted vs dedicated).
- Automate sampling + one-click revert in Console for common experiments. (EO: Jonas)
- Establish eviction policy for long-running slices (>30d) to avoid unnoticed drift.

Appendix: small scenarios
1) Model A increases P95 by 40% at 2% slice but success rate unchanged -> reduce slice to 0.5% and enable warm-cache prefetch, re-evaluate.
2) Hallucination score spikes at 0.5% -> immediate rollback and targeted manual review of sampled responses; hold on re-release until fixes.

Notes-to-self style observations
- Keep step sizes conservative when changing quantization or kernel paths; those have non-linear perf/quality tradeoffs.
- It helps to run a simultaneous synthetic traffic harness when bumping to 10%+ to saturate cache warming quickly.

This is a living working doc. Pull requests welcome to expand product-line specifics and automate routine bits.
